To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the logarithmic divergences of one-loop lattice Feyman integrals are universal and that they can be calculated by the continuum methods.

logarithmically UV-divergent lattice Feynman diagrams are universal in the sense of being independent of the details of the lattice discretization, and that the continuum limit of such diagrams is equal to the corresponding diagram in the continuum, regularized, for example, by a momentum cut-off.

logarithmically-divergent one-loop lattice Feyman integrals are of the general form I(a,p,M) = f(p)(log(aM) + const) + g(p,M), where the f(p) is the corresponding continuum function and the g(p,M) is a finite function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of Feynman diagrams in quantum field theory.
the calculation of one-loop lattice Feyman integrals, and the general properties of such integrals.
the calculation of the one-loop Feynman diagrams for the quantum electrodynamics (QED) in the presence of the lattice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
logarithmic divergences in one-loop lattice Feynamn integrals are universal in the sense that the logarithmic divergent part is the same as the corresponding continuum integral.
the lattice QCD one-loop beta-function and renormalization constants are independent of the lattice action and lattice spacing up to terms which are higher order in the lattice spacing.
the one-loop logarithmic divergence of a lattice Feynman integral is the same as that of the corresponding continuum integral.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lattice Feynman integral is not only a good approximation for the continuum Feynman integral in the limit of vanishing lattice spacing but also a good approximation for its renormalization properties.
the lattice Feynman integral is the lattice version of the corresponding continuum Feynman integral.
the lattice Feynman integral is a lattice regularized version of its continuum counterpart.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the logarithmic divergences of the lattice Feynman integral I(p,a) are independent of the regularization of the continuum integral I(p,epsilon) for epsilon -> 0, where epsilon is the cut-off parameter.
one-loop Feynman integrands on the lattice are not as complicated as they may first appear.
one can compute the one-loop beta-function and the renormalization group functions of the quark and gluon fields, and of the quark bilinear operators, directly from lattice Feynman diagrams.
